endorsements.quote: Moving forward, conversations should continue to include a multitude of stakeholders—patients, clinicians, advocacy bodies, policy makers, and technologists—but it is still not clear if discussions will provide meaningful resolution to a host of ongoing concerns surrounding explainability, trustworthiness, open-data, privacy, and machine learning.
Involving patients in this discussion is critical—even if it might seem to slow progress or muddy the risk vs. utility calculation.

unlisted_practices: Apply model-guided k-anonymity or other anonymisation techniques to training datasets and models before publishing them, to reduce patient re-identification risk.
Apply data minimisation to AI models by re-evaluating after training which input features can be generalised or removed without reducing accuracy, and document cases where all data is required.
Conduct a Privacy Impact Assessment extended to ethics, society, and law domains during the AI development lifecycle, and carry it out in a public and open manner.
Apply additional anonymisation safeguards to multi-modal datasets released openly.

screen.reason: This is a brief report/commentary outlining governance, privacy risk mitigation, informed consent, and ethical tensions in the iToBoS project rather than an empirical evaluation.
